title: Buffer Solutions Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Add one drop of acid to pure water and its pH crashes. Add the same drop to blood and the pH barely moves. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Aarav races his bicycle up a steep road, his muscles make acid, yet his blood stays at about pH 7.4.

Think of a goal with two keepers: one catches acid, one catches base. On the molecule bench you will add 0.01 mol of hydrochloric acid to one litre of pure water (pH 7 to 2) and to an acetic acid and sodium acetate buffer (pH 4.76 to 4.67) and watch acetate catch the protons. We cover acidic buffers (about pH 4.75) and basic buffers (about pH 9.25), derive the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation pH = pKa + log [salt]/[acid] step by step, do basic buffers with pOH, see how blood uses carbonic acid and hydrogen carbonate, pause to compare two buffers, work out a buffer of 0.1 M acid and 0.2 M salt (pH 5.06), show the flipped-ratio trap, then an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 69 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
